svg.title: B17 / AQUARIUS LIFELINE — Inland Fisheries Resilience engineering mission profile
svg.desc: B17, AQUARIUS LIFELINE — Inland Fisheries Resilience. Original project: Off the Hook: Assessing the Vulnerability of Inland Subsistence Fisheries to Climate Change. Session B: Earth & Environmental Engineering. Scientific question: Which climate and access stresses most threaten dependable subsistence harvest, and which feasible adaptations reduce downside risk? Testable hypothesis: Seasonal hydrologic extremes combined with high dietary dependence and constrained alternatives may matter more than annual mean warming alone; adaptation effects will differ among households and governance systems.. svg.text: Off the Hook: Assessing the Vulnerability of Inland Subsistence Fisheries to Climate Change
No project observations acquired · specified cases await execution · shared demonstrations are separately labeled
Assess climate vulnerability as the interaction of aquatic exposure,
ecological sensitivity and household dependence, with local knowledge and
governance central to interpretation. Build a transparent scenario model for
one consented basin before scaling. Avoid reducing communities to a
universal vulnerability score or equating fishery-production changes with
Which climate and access stresses most threaten dependable subsistence
harvest, and which feasible adaptations reduce downside risk?
TESTABLE HYPOTHESIS / NOT AN OBSERVED RESULT
Seasonal hydrologic extremes combined with high dietary dependence and
constrained alternatives may matter more than annual mean warming alone;
adaptation effects will differ among households and governance systems.
Recorded catch may omit informal/subsistence harvest.
Effort and catchability change with climate, access and gear.
Community/Indigenous data rights govern collection, linkage and release.
VALIDITY LIMITS / THE CLAIM STOPS HERE
Species composition and informal catch may be poorly observed. Scenario
uncertainty and nonclimate stresses such as dams or access restrictions can
dominate; composite weights reflect values as well as evidence.
COUNTS OF RECORDS · NO COMPLETION SCORES
TRACEABILITY / IDs THAT STAY WITH THE WORK
Execution evidence is required before case closure.
